title: Flagged for review
description: Irregularities, unresolved verification items and open decisions. Nothing here blocks deployment — the brief is explicit that flagged items are published for after-the-fact review — and nothing here is a to-do we quietly did anyway. Each item says what a reviewer must decide or verify, and links the official source that settles it.

rows.item: Repository contained no data, code, schema or tests
rows.detail: At the commit this branch started from, the repo held exactly one file: README.md, 6 bytes, contents '# FL1'. The brief reads as though a data project existed; it did not. Every requirement is therefore greenfield, and there was no prior work to verify.
rows.reviewer_action: Confirm no earlier repository or branch was intended to be the starting point; if one exists, this project should be re-scoped against it.

rows.detail: No LICENSE file existed, so default copyright applied and any reuse or collaboration was legally undefined. An MIT LICENSE was added in this branch.
rows.reviewer_action: Keep MIT, or name the licence you want (or none) and it will be replaced.

rows.detail: Absent, so a static build plus Python would commit __pycache__, duplicate build output and editor files. Added in this branch.
GET repos/sassnix321/FL1/pages returned 404 at claim time; the repo had no homepage URL.
rows.reviewer_action: After deployment, confirm the published URL and the source branch shown in Settings → Pages.

rows.item: No live NFL data existed anywhere in the repo
rows.detail: There was no ingestion pipeline, so any 'finding' written into a table would necessarily have been an invention. This is why the site's tables are registers of sourced rules, gaps and methods rather than numbers.
rows.reviewer_action: Accept that the first numbers arrive with the first licensed data, or fund that licence (S-01).

rows.item: Git author identity differs from the repository owner handle
rows.detail: Commits are authored by sassnix321-star <sassnix321@gmail.com> in a repo owned by sassnix321. Cosmetic, but it is the kind of mismatch worth a five-second check that no other identity is involved.
rows.reviewer_action: Confirm the git author and the GitHub account are both you.

rows.item: Four sessions claimed the same scope
rows.detail: This branch plus three sibling branches were all created from the same commit, and each wrote a COORDINATION.md claiming every task — because when each wrote its board, it could see only itself. Two siblings have a board and nothing else; one built a complete site.
rows.reviewer_action: Decide the intended division of labour. This branch merged all three siblings additively rather than overwriting them; a different split can be re-cut without losing any of it.

rows.item: Sibling site uses a weaker verification standard than the brief
rows.detail: The site built on arena/89c32e23-fl1 labels rows 'Verified (source reachable)' for nfl.com/injuries and nfl.com/standings. Reachability is not verification of a value: the brief requires a source per row, meaning the row's content was read at the source. Their tables are otherwise correctly left blank, and their flagged page honestly lists the gaps (U-01…U-07).
rows.reviewer_action: Accept the merge as-is and treat 'reachable' as a weaker tier, or ask that their two 'Verified (source reachable)' rows be relabelled. Nothing was deleted and no value was invented.

rows.item: Sibling site states 'no manual data input' while no ingestion exists
rows.detail: Its landing page says 'Built without manual data input'. The site is hand-authored HTML with deliberately blank tables; no pipeline ingests anything, so the sentence describes intent rather than mechanism.
rows.reviewer_action: Either add the collector (blocked on a host: Q-19, GAP-18) or soften the claim.

rows.detail: Both the sibling site and this build publish an index at docs/. Resolved additively: the sibling site stays at the Pages root as the narrative front door, this build's pages live under docs/pages/, and both are cross-linked. It is not a duplicate of content — one is prose-and-blanks, the other is generated from the registers — but two indexes is a decision, not an accident.
rows.reviewer_action: Choose one: keep the two-tier structure, or promote docs/pages/index.html to the root and retire the other index to a section page.

sections.title: B. Verification items: official paths that do not exist
sections.description: Each of these was an expected official source that is not where the internet says it is. Recorded because a later session will otherwise repeat the search, and because the absence changes the design.

rows.found: The league's '404 - Flag on the Play' page, fetched in this session
rows.impact: The brief's 2nd/3rd/4th-string requirement cannot be sourced from the league site as assumed. The deficiency index now derives the replacement from roster-eligibility rules plus our own snap-share estimate, labelled as an estimate.
rows.needs: Either 32 club-site parsers, or a documented decision to use the derived shadow chart permanently.

rows.found: Redirects to the club directory (all 32 teams, no transactions)
rows.impact: Roster-move evidence must be taken from club pages or the league's news feed, with per-club parsing rather than one endpoint.
rows.needs: Locate the current transactions endpoint and record it in the source register.

rows.found: Both return the NFL 404 page; the operations homepage instead exposes a '2026 NFL RULEBOOK' entry point
rows.impact: Rules citations must be rebuilt from live navigation. The injury-report *definitions* were sourced from the league's Competition Committee release instead, which is citable.
rows.needs: Pin the 2026 rulebook URL and the current injury-report policy text into the register.

rows.expected: Nevada Gaming Control Board revenue-report landing pages
rows.found: Two plausible paths on gaming.nv.gov returned a plain '404 Not Found'; only a direct monthly-report PDF path is evidenced, and only via a search index
rows.impact: No Nevada hold percentage is published anywhere in this project, including the widely-quoted parlay-card figures. The hold gate (G-7) is therefore BLOCKED, not passed.
rows.needs: Open the monthly report PDF (or the correct landing page) and record the sports and parlay-card win percentages with the report period.

rows.expected: An official league endpoint for the final inactive list
rows.found: Not identified in this pass; the game-status report is verified, the Sunday list is not
rows.impact: The Sunday re-price step of the model is specified but unverified; our committed number is the Friday report until this is settled.
rows.needs: Find the official gameday-operations reference for inactive-list timing, then instrument a timestamped capture job.

rows.found: Bibliographic record confirmed across three independent reference lists (Bell System Technical Journal 35(4):917-926); no publisher URL was confirmed, and one guessed domain does not exist
rows.impact: The staking section cites the citation, not a link. Deliberate: a dead or invented DOI on a page whose standard is 'no hallucinations' would be worse than no DOI.
rows.needs: Locate the publisher's archival link and update the register row.

rows.expected: Verification of the academic papers cited for market inefficiency
rows.found: Most were verified at abstract or reference-list level through publisher pages (Springer link fetched in full for one); paywalled bodies were not read
rows.impact: Those findings are used as *motivation* for signals, never as coefficients or thresholds. Each is labelled accordingly in the source register.
rows.needs: Read the papers properly before any of their effect sizes is used to set a gate threshold.

rows.expected: Roster rules current for the 2026 league year
rows.found: The official roster-FAQ article is written around the 2022 league year (it still discusses suspended COVID protocols)
rows.impact: Every roster constant (four-game IR minimum, eight designations, 47/48 gameday active) is marked 'as-described 2022' and must be re-confirmed before it is coded.
rows.needs: Read the 2026 rulebook and the current CBA summary; update the register.

sections.title: C. Decisions that are not ours to make
sections.description: The brief says there should be no manual input from you. These are the items where stopping is the correct behaviour: each one requires money, a licence, a legal opinion, or an account, and an agent that 'decided' them would be manufacturing a mandate.

rows.decision: Buy a licensed historical lines feed
rows.why_an_agent_cannot_make_it: It is a purchase with recurring cost and a contract that limits what we may publish. Everything analytical is blocked behind it.
It changes the legal, tax and safety profile of the entire project. The repo has no bankroll policy or jurisdiction, so there is nothing to infer from.
Prize, chance and consideration is a regulated combination. The design is ready with non-cash rewards; the legal question belongs to counsel.
They encode loss tolerance. The engine ships conservative defaults (quarter-Kelly, 2% cap, exposure clustering) precisely so that no one has to guess on your behalf.

rows.decision: Provision a host for the collector
rows.why_an_agent_cannot_make_it: Requires credentials and a bill. This sandbox has no outbound access to the league or the regulators, which is why ingestion is written and unit-tested but has never run against a live page.

rows.decision: Scraping policy for club and league pages
rows.why_an_agent_cannot_make_it: The league's data estate is exclusively distributed, so 'just scrape it' is a legal and durability question, not an engineering preference.
It is an organisational decision about who owns the published site. This session merged additively and changed no sibling file; the alternative splits are yours to choose.
